translationRepairs: At Yongyuan's end he became Secretariat staff aide.
At Yongyuan's end he became staff aide to the Minister of Education.
s0017 遷司徒行參軍 names staff aide under the Situ (Minister of Education), not the Secretariat (尚書); the proposed idiomatic restores the correct office.
Gao Di heard and sent a Secretariat Attendant to comfort him, then issued an edict: "Forward Army Shen Chongsu showed resolve young and mourning beyond measure.
Gaozu heard and sent a Secretariat Attendant to comfort him, then issued an edict: "Forward Army Shen Chongsu showed resolve young and mourning beyond measure.
s0029 高祖 is the temple name Gaozu; idiomatic “Gao Di” invents a different title and conflicts with the Chinese and the literal Gaozu.
Commandery and county reported; Gao Di sent a Secretariat Attendant to release mourning and make him Left Regular Attendant in Prince of Yuzhang's kingdom.
Commandery and county reported; Gaozu sent a Secretariat Attendant to release mourning and make him Left Regular Attendant in Prince of Yuzhang's kingdom.
s0048 高祖詔遣 again has temple name Gaozu; replacing “Gao Di” corrects the same naming error.
Gao Di was moved and ordered Minister of Justice Cai Fadu: "Ji Bin asks to die for his father—his loyalty is admirable;
Gaozu was moved and ordered Minister of Justice Cai Fadu: "Ji Bin asks to die for his father—his loyalty is admirable;
s0088 高祖異之 is Gaozu; “Gao Di” is not supported by the Chinese.
Fadu saw Chong's heart could not be broken; he softened and said, "The throne knows your father is innocent and will free him soon.
Fadu saw Bin's heart could not be broken; he softened and said, "The throne knows your father is innocent and will free him soon.
s0101 法度知翂 names Ji Bin (翂); English “Chong” is a wrong given name, likely confusion with Shen Chongsu.
Fadu knew Chong's resolve was fixed and could not be bent; he changed to gentle persuasion and said, "The emperor knows your honored father is guiltless and will soon release him.
Fadu knew Bin's resolve was fixed and could not be bent; he changed to gentle persuasion and said, "The emperor knows your honored father is guiltless and will soon release him.
The same 翂 in s0101 must be Bin in the literal; Chong is unsupported.
Chong answered, "Even minnows and ants cling to life;
Bin answered, "Even minnows and ants cling to life;
s0104 翂對曰 attributes the speech to Bin; Chong is a naming error.
Chong replied, "Even fish fry and ants cherish their lives;
Bin replied, "Even fish fry and ants cherish their lives;
Literal s0104 likewise has 翂; Bin is required.
When Chong entered prison the clerks, by statute, fitted him with every bond;
When Bin entered prison the clerks, by statute, fitted him with every bond;
s0108 翂初見囚 refers to Bin entering prison; Chong is wrong.
When Chong was first imprisoned the jailers, by law, loaded him with full shackles;
When Bin was first imprisoned the jailers, by law, loaded him with full shackles;
Literal s0108 has the same 翂; Bin restores the correct name.
Chong refused: "I seek to die for my father—a man under death sentence should wear more, not less?"
Bin refused: "I seek to die for my father—a man under death sentence should wear more, not less?"
s0110 翂弗聽 / 翂求代父死 names Bin twice; Chong is invented.
Chong would not agree and said, "I ask to die for my father—a capital convict should only have bonds added; how may they be lessened?"
Bin would not agree and said, "I ask to die for my father—a capital convict should only have bonds added; how may they be lessened?"
Literal s0110 repeats 翂; Bin is the correct given name.
Chong said, "Strange, Magistrate Wang—how little you think of Chong!
Bin said, "Strange, Magistrate Wang—how little you think of Bin!
s0114 翂曰…何量翂之薄乎 uses Bin’s given name in both the narrator and the quoted self-reference; Chong is wrong.
Chong said, "How strange, Magistrate Wang—how shallow you judge Chong!
Bin said, "How strange, Magistrate Wang—how shallow you judge Bin!
Literal s0114 has the same double 翂; both must read Bin.
Later Pei Jian of his town, Zang Dun of Dan'yang, and Zhang Ze, Yangzhou rectifier, jointly praised Chong's pure filiality and clear grasp of the Changes and Laozi.
Later Pei Jian of his town, Zang Dun of Dan'yang, and Zhang Ze, Yangzhou rectifier, jointly praised Bin's pure filiality and clear grasp of the Changes and Laozi.
s0121 連名薦翂 recommends Bin; Chong is a mistranslation of 翂.

Later townsman Pei Jian, Dan'yang assistant magistrate Zang Dun, and Yangzhou rectifier Zhang Ze jointly recommended Chong, finding his filial conduct pure and his mastery of the Changes and Laozi clear.

Later townsman Pei Jian, Dan'yang assistant magistrate Zang Dun, and Yangzhou rectifier Zhang Ze jointly recommended Bin, finding his filial conduct pure and his mastery of the Changes and Laozi clear.
Literal s0121 likewise recommends 翂 (Bin), not Chong.
If Chong had face to live, having done this act, it would be buying fame through one's father—how shameful!"
If Bin had face to live, having done this act, it would be buying fame through one's father—how shameful!"
s0116 若翂有靦面目 continues Bin’s speech with his given name; Chong is unsupported.
At the start of Heavenly Surveillance Xiao Dan, Prince of Shixing and inspector, reported him.
At the start of Tianjian, Xiao Dan, Prince of Shixing and inspector, reported him.
天監 is the reign-era Tianjian, not “Heavenly Surveillance”; a comma after Tianjian is also needed so the era is not fused with the personal name Xiao Dan.
Early in Heavenly Surveillance the inspector, Prince of Shixing Xiao Dan, memorialized him.
Early in Tianjian the inspector, Prince of Shixing Xiao Dan, memorialized him.
Literal “Heavenly Surveillance” calques 天監; the reign-era name is Tianjian, and the proposed wording is accurate.
Jiang Gou, styled Hanjie, was from Kaocheng in Jiyang.
Jiang Fou, styled Hanjie, was from Kaocheng in Jiyang.
Gou is a wrong reading of 紑, but the standard reading is fóu (Fou), not Fu (fú); the biography header must use Fou.
Jiang Gou, styled Hanjie, was a man of Kaocheng in Jiyang.
Jiang Fou, styled Hanjie, was a man of Kaocheng in Jiyang.
Literal likewise needs Fou for 紑; Gou is wrong and Fu misstates the reading.
In Tianjian he began as court gentleman, rose to staff equal on the Prince of Jin'an of Xuanhui's staff with inner recorder duties, then magistrate of Xichang.
In Tianjian he began as court gentleman for attendance, rose to staff equal on the Xuanhui staff of the Prince of Jin'an with concurrent inner-recorder duties, then went out as magistrate of Xichang.

宣惠晉安王府參軍 is staff equal on the Xuanhui (general’s title) staff of the Prince of Jin’an; “Prince of Jin’an of Xuanhui” reverses that structure. The proposed wording also correctly expands 奉朝請, 兼, and 出補.

In the Tianjian era he first entered office as court gentleman for attendance, then was promoted staff equal on the staff of the Prince of Xuanhui of Jin'an, concurrently inner recorder within limits, and went out to supplement magistrate of Xichang.

In the Tianjian era he first entered office as court gentleman for attendance, then was promoted staff equal on the Xuanhui staff of the Prince of Jin'an, concurrently inner recorder within limits, and went out to fill the post of magistrate of Xichang.
Literal “Prince of Xuanhui of Jin’an” misreads 宣惠 as the princely title; 宣惠 modifies the staff and 晉安王 is the prince. The proposed repair restores that order.
He became magistrate of Jiankang, which he did not enjoy.
He became rectifier of Jiankang, which he did not enjoy.
s0235 建康正 is the Jiankang rectifier; s0237’s later 建康令 shows magistrate is a distinct office, so “magistrate” here is wrong.
He returned and became magistrate of Jiankang—not to his liking.
He returned and became rectifier of Jiankang—not to his liking.
Literal likewise mistakes 正 for 令; rectifier matches 建康正.
Xiaoxu often said, "He is our house's Yang element."
Xiaoxu often said, "He is our house's Yangyuan."
吾家陽元也 compares Xie Lan to the style-name Yangyuan (陽元), not a metaphysical “Yang element.”
Xiaoxu often said, "He is the Yang element of our house."
Xiaoxu often said, "He is the Yangyuan of our house."
Literal “Yang element” is the same mistranslation of the personal style 陽元; Yangyuan is required.
When mourning for his father ended he wailed day and night, wasted away until only bone stood, and his mother Lady Ruan constantly watched over him herself to restrain and comfort him.
When he entered mourning for his father he wailed day and night, wasted away until only bone stood, and his mother Lady Ruan constantly watched over him herself to restrain and comfort him.
及丁父憂 marks entering mourning for his father; “when mourning ended” contradicts both 丁憂 and the following 服闋後 in s0263.

When sweet dew fell on the Scholars' Grove Lan presented a eulogy the emperor praised; he was ordered to compose the stele on Xiao Kai's virtuous rule in North Yanzhou and the eulogy on the Prince of Xuancheng presenting the Mean.

When sweet dew fell on the Scholars' Grove, Lan presented a eulogy the emperor praised; he was ordered to compose the stele on Xiao Kai's virtuous rule in North Yanzhou and the eulogy on the Prince of Xuancheng presenting the Mean.
士林館，藺獻頌 separates the place from the subject Lan; without the comma, “Scholars' Grove Lan” fuses place and personal name and obscures who presented the eulogy.
